metadataOnly: Ships with no walked line, stages or waypoints: the confirmed relation 19693803 holds 2.06 km of a roughly 170 km route in two components 22.3 km apart, and the corridor sweep found nowhere near enough to join them. See the osm block.

description.en: 170 km coastal route from Ise Grand Shrine to Kumano Hayatama Taisha. A series of 20+ mountain passes connecting fishing villages along the eastern coast of the Kii Peninsula. Typically 9-14 days.

distanceNote.en: 170 km is the scoping figure this pilgrimage's own design spec sets for the Iseji (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-pilgrimages-and-sections-design.md, section 5.2, which also expects about nine stages), and the same figure the March 2026 variant stub this section was promoted from already carried. It is not measured against a walked line, because none exists: OpenStreetMap relation 19693803 holds 2.06 km of a roughly 170 km route, and the corridor sweep found nowhere near enough to assemble the rest — see the osm block. The 9-14 day range beside it came from that same stub with no source of its own. Expect both to be corrected once the section is cut.

elevationRange.elevationNote: Sea level to 647 m was carried over unchanged from the March 2026 routes/kumano-kodo/variants/iseji stub, whose one provenance entry claimed OpenStreetMap geometry this repository has never held. Nothing here has measured it: there is no walked line to sample and no elevation model has been run over this corridor. It is kept as a declared figure, and it is the 647 m the Kohechi's page compares its own high point against. The stub's totalAscentMeters (5,000) and totalDescentMeters (5,020) were removed rather than annotated: cumulative ascent and descent are quantities you derive from a line, this section has none, and two round unsourced numbers read as measurements of a profile nobody took. They come back when the line does.

sources.name: This repository's own planning
sources.notes: distanceKm, estimatedDays and elevationRange are declared figures, not measurements: their origins are recorded in overview.distanceNote and overview.elevationRange.elevationNote. The OpenStreetMap entry below covers the relation lookup and nothing else.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap
sources.notes: Relation 19693803 is the confirmed Iseji — see the osm block below for why it is pinned even though no walked line ships from it this release.

osm.note: Confirmed as the Iseji: wikidata=Q11379141, wikipedia=ja:伊勢路 (熊野古道), and website=https://www.kodo.pref.mie.lg.jp/, Mie Prefecture's own Kumano Kodō site. Pinned here even though this section ships without geometry, so the next attempt starts from a confirmed id rather than repeating a day of research. The relation holds only two ways, 2.06 km total against a roughly 170 km route: 120679201 (1.32 km, 136.20 E / 34.09 N, in the hills above Owase) and 1128207928 (0.74 km, 136.11 E / 33.90 N, above Kumano-shi). Each length is paired with its own place from that way's own node coordinates, not from the order the two are listed in. Their nearest ends are 22.3 km apart. That is an upstream OpenStreetMap gap, not a wrong id: a corridor-wide sweep for the classic Iseji pass names turns up only about 10 km more of loose, unrelated ways, nowhere near enough to assemble a walked line. ways: null until OpenStreetMap fills in what is missing.
